grammarPoint.title: -(으)ㅁ (written nominalization)
grammarPoint.hint: Turn a clause into a formal noun-like statement.
grammarPoint.description: In formal writing, -(으)ㅁ turns an action or state into a noun-like clause that can serve as the object of reporting, confirmation or explanation. It often appears in notices, reports and official writing.

notes.title: Build it step by step
notes.content: For a stem ending in a consonant, attach 음; after a vowel add ㅁ: 읽다 → 읽음, 가다 → 감. Past endings can be included: 끝나다 → 끝났음; then add a particle as needed (끝났음을).

notes.title: Worked example
notes.content: 회의가 끝났음을 확인했습니다. — We confirmed that the meeting had ended. 끝나다 becomes 끝났음 as a formal nominal clause, then takes 을 to mark what was confirmed.

notes.title: Common trap
notes.content: This is common in official writing rather than casual conversation. Compare -기 nominalization for activities and -는 것 for noun-like clauses in everyday language.

lessonExamples.englishHint: We confirmed that the meeting had ended.
We emphasized that safety is important.

cards.englishHint: We inform you that the documents are required.
We confirmed that the problem was resolved.
We recorded that everyone had agreed.
